theorem falls_to_unmet {hi : Nat} (nothing : RegimeMargin.FromNothing giving) (keeps : RegimeMargin.Keeps giving 0 hi) (grows : ∀ u, use u < taken use (kids u)) (down : ∀ u v, v ∈ kids u → need v ≤ need u) {w : List U} {x : Nat} (needs : Needing need kids w) (high : x ≤ hi) (ne : w ≠ []) (met : ∀ u, u ∈ w → need u ≤ x) : ∃ n, 0 < n ∧ n ≤ hi + 1 ∧ (∀ j, j < n → ∀ u, u ∈ (course need kids giving use (w, x) j).1 → need u ≤ (course need kids giving use (w, x) j).2) ∧ (∀ j, j ≤ n → (course need kids giving use (w, x) j).1 = generation kids j w) ∧ (∃ u, u ∈ (course need kids giving use (w, x) n).1 ∧ (course need kids giving use (w, x) n).2 < need u) ∧ (∃ p, p ∈ w ∧ need p ≤ x ∧ (course need kids giving use (w, x) n).2 < need p) ∧ (course need kids giving use (w, x) n).2 < x

falls_to_unmet docstring: "**A way whose kids take more, its kids needing no more than their parent, comes within `hi + 1` steps to a level below a need the start met.** The premises are `need_unmet`'s (`nothing`, `keeps`, `grows` asked of every unit of the type, `needs` asked only of the descendants of `w`, `high`, `ne`, `met`), with kids needing no more than their parent (`down`). There is a step `n` with `0 < n ≤ hi + 1` such that every need is met at every step before `n`; up to `n` the way at step `j` is `generation kids j w`, in which no giving, use or level appears: it is the way of every course from `w` on which every need is met until then (`way_while_met`), and what it takes rises at each of those steps (by `generations_rise` read through that conjunct; not itself a conjunct); some unit of the way at `n` has its need unmet; some unit of `w`, whose need the start met, needs more than the level at `n`; and the level at `n` is below the start level `x`. By `need_unmet`, and `generation_ancestor` for the unit of `w` whose need is at least the unmet one. This is the model's form of a going-on that draws down what it rests on while nothing in it yet differs (a reading). Given, not derived: the needs, uses and offspring; that each unit's kids together take more than it (`grows`); the cap (`keeps`, `high`); `down`."

need_unmet docstring (the "uses up" sentence removed): "**A need comes to be unmet, the way unchanged by the stock until then.** With nothing given from nothing (`nothing`), the step under no draw keeping every level up to `hi` within `hi` (`keeps`), every unit's kids taking more than it (`grows`, asked of every unit of the type), every unit of every generation of `w` needing something (`needs`, asked only of the descendants of `w`), the start at most `hi` (`high`), a way that is not empty (`ne`) and every need met at the start (`met`): there is a step `n` with `0 < n ≤ hi + 1` at which some unit of the way has its need unmet, every need met at every step before it, and up to it the way at step `j` is the `j`-th generation of `w` (`way_while_met`). Were every need met up to `hi + 1`, the course would be the course as it was under `allKids` (`course_asItWas`), what it takes rising at each step (`generations_rise`), and its level at `hi + 1` nothing (`TurningInTime.rising_takes_all`), while a unit there needs something. Kids needing no more than their parent (`down`) is not asked, and without it the unmet need may be a kid's greater need at a level that has not fallen: on `KidHigherNeed` every premise holds at `hi = 12`, and the configuration after the first step is `([B, B], 12)`, its level the start's, below `B`'s need thirteen. With `down` the level has fallen below a need the start met (`falls_to_unmet`). `ends_high` rests on the same arithmetic, a take that rises against a capped level, for a line among other units, argued again there; of the laws here only `need_unmet` and those derived from it (`falls_to_unmet`, `one_need_ends`) rest on `TurningInTime.rising_takes_all`."

Module bullet: "* **A way whose kids take more comes to an unmet need within `hi + 1` steps, the way until then not depending on the stock** (`need_unmet`): with nothing given from nothing and the step under no draw keeping every level up to `hi` within `hi` (`RegimeMargin.Keeps giving 0 hi`), a way that is not empty, starting at most `hi`, every unit's kids taking more (asked of every unit) and every descendant of the way needing something, every need met at the start, comes to an unmet need at a step from 1 to `hi + 1`; up to it the way is the generation, in which no giving, use or level appears (`way_while_met`).
